proj_launchpad: Improving Underwriting Efficiency Through Behaviour-Driven Design
Turning user data into a smarter navigation model + dynamic view port to provide a better decision environment
An internal underwriting application for insurance teams to review and triage submissions, manage workflows, and make faster and more confident decisions
An internal underwriting application for insurance teams to review and triage submissions, manage workflows, and make faster and more confident decisions
Usage at a glance (in a typical month):
Total time spent of active usage
Underwriters work in a high-volume, high-stakes environment where speed and accuracy are essential. The application’s workflow centered around two primary pages:
Pipeline View : A table-based workspace for filtering, triaging, and updating submissions
Submission Detail : A deep-dive view containing full submission context, documents, analysis, and activity history
As the sole product designer brought in to shape the next version of this product, I began with a structured UX audit to identify improvement opportunities.
Following the UX audit, I analysed the funnel behaviour, heat maps, feature usage and session data to understand how underwriters actually worked.
What information do users need during triage?
How can the interface better support comparison across submissions?
Are users navigating efficiently or compensating for missing context?
1. Only 46.1% of users entered the submission detail page
2. The Back button was the most-used interaction on submission detail
3. Users frequently looped between pipeline and submission detail
4. Submission detail was used selectively to access specific context, especially summaries and notes
The answer: fast comprehension first, depth on demand
The pipeline view functioned as the true decision workspace, while the submission detail page acted as a short-term inspection layer.
Underwriters relied on the pipeline page for orientation and comparison, opening submission detail primarily to verify context before returning to continue their review.
1. Rebalanced information hierarchy to surface key signals closer to the pipeline
2. Cut navigation overhead with pre-filtered views and a 'filters-on-demand' system
3. Introduced a contextual Details drawer for files, AI insights, activity history, and notes
4. Implemented an adaptive viewport to support dense data analysis without losing workflow context
I proposed a design direction that improved the workflow and resolved key UX friction points:

I designed a ‘filters-on-demand’ system that reduced visual complexity while maintaining flexibility. Frequently used filters were prioritised, and reusable filter presets allowed underwriters to quickly re-establish context across sessions.
I proposed consolidating key submission information into a contextual drawer accessible from the pipeline page.
To accommodate high-density data, I designed an adaptive viewport that supports uninterrupted data analysis while preserving quick access to workflow context and collaboration tools.
With over 224 hours of monthly usage, even small improvements could scale quickly. Reducing just one minute per session could save over 45 hours per month across underwriting teams.
Due to roadmap priorities, this work was positioned as a future optimisation, establishing a clear, data-backed direction for improving underwriting efficiency at scale.

An internal underwriting application for insurance teams to review and triage submissions, manage workflows, and make faster and more confident decisions
During busy renewal periods, underwriters analyse hundreds of reinsurance and insurance contracts under tight deadlines. Their workflow is chaotic—constantly switching between:
Make contract review instantaneous, not time-consuming
Simplify checking against complex underwriting rules
Reduce compliance risk and financial exposure
How might we accelerate contract analysis without compromising thoroughness, accuracy, or user confidence in AI-generated insights?
I conducted stakeholder interviews with underwriters and product managers to understand their workflows, pain points, and needs during high-pressure renewal periods.
Navigation must be instantaneous and mirror document’s natural flow
Users question AI accuracy, design should communicate transparency and verifiable sources
AI assistance should feel like productive work, not extra overhead
I went through three distinct layout approaches, testing each with PMs and users to land on the optimal information hierarchy that also fit within the dev team's technical constraints.
This is what the UI looked like when I first joined the project.
Rebalanced the information hierarchy across multiple layers of detail
Consolidated all detailed information in a modal to minimise visual noise
(blocked by dev team due to tech constrains)
Parent accordions organised by document section (mirroring contract order)
Enable users to do side-by-side comparison with one click
Detected wording is compared against preferred language in a clear side-by-side view with concise risk summaries, enabling decisions in seconds.

Underwriters can quickly verify or relink AI-detected text within the “Text” view, embedding feedback directly into their normal review workflow. Each correction improves model accuracy over time, ensuring the system evolves with real user judgement.
Key validation actions are surfaced at the point of review, enabling one-step decisions and preserving underwriters’ analytical flow.

Instead of jumping between components to recall what needs discussion, underwriters get a consolidated view of every flagged item, suggested alternative, and comment at a glance. When everything checks out, a single 'Finish Validation' click closes the loop.

jcdcasestudy: Direct access to end users is unavailable
How their product look like before

While our client has great and insightful content, accessibility issues such as a lack of visual cues and other UX concerns, like an unclear value proposition in the hero section, may lead users to feel confused during interactions with the product. Additionally, it is not easy for them to stay engaged.
The client is a global outdoor advertising company that wants to leverage the digital hub to attract and inspire experts to build their marketing cases.
Help the client redesign their content hub to attract more visitors, inspiring them to explore our client's services and build cases based on the content.
To assist our clients in securing more deals, we have been assigned the task of crafting an inclusive and intuitive user experience to elevate overall user engagement.
- New hero section with clear CTA that invites users to explore further - A delightful signup progress

We conducted a UX audit to address usability issues, heuristic problems, and pain points. Given the deadline and limited resources for conducting additional user research, a UX audit is the best way to identify design opportunities.
After synthesising our research findings, we identified three major UX problems on the previous content hub.
Unclear Value Proposition in Hero Section
Users lack a clear understanding of what the content hub offers and how it meets their needs, leading to a potentially high bouncing rate.
The absence of filtering and sorting features hinders users from locating their desired content.
Additionally, the product lacks personalized content, further limiting the user experience.
The client has really great and desirable content, however due to the lacking visual cues of interactive contents and contents hosting layers of information, users cannot explore further.
To address reduced satisfaction when users select diverse content types during onboarding, we explored creating a simple and interactive onboarding process and found the best solution.
We held varying opinions on the podcast episode page UI. To decide, we conducted a brief dot voting process and chose the design that prioritizes consistency.
A dynamic and engaling user experience
- Design with mobile optimization in mind
By transforming the podcasts page into an interactive and visually appealing hub, we anticipate an increase in user engagement, longer session durations, and higher retention rates.
After completing Immersion, we were re-engaged by the client to build the MVP!!!
